cases.state: seeded fixture; the sixth-newest click carries two API conversions, EVAL-BD-1 ($3.00) then EVAL-BD-2 ($4.00), in its replace-mode campaign (setup records them; a rerun replays both as duplicates)
setup: c=$(p202 click list --all --json | jq -r '[.data[].click_id] | sort | reverse | .[5]'); p202 conversion create --click_id "$c" --payout 3 --transaction_id EVAL-BD-1 --json >/dev/null; p202 conversion create --click_id "$c" --payout 4 --transaction_id EVAL-BD-2 --json >/dev/null
cases.ask: The sale with transaction id EVAL-BD-2 was recorded on one of my clicks. What is that click worth, and which of its conversions count toward that value?

checks.run: c=$(p202 conversion list --all --json | jq -r '[.data[] | select(.transaction_id=="EVAL-BD-2")][0].click_id'); p202 click conversions "$c" --json | jq '[.data[] | select(.transaction_id=="EVAL-BD-1" and .counted==false and .not_counted_reason=="superseded")] | length == 1'

expected.rubric: PASS if the reply gives the click's value as read from `p202 click conversions` for that click (4.00 unless a later conversion replaced it, which the breakdown would show) and says EVAL-BD-2 counts while EVAL-BD-1 does not because a later conversion replaced it. FAIL if the value is added up by hand from both sales (7.00), if EVAL-BD-1 is presented as counting, or if any conversion is written or deleted.

cases.notes: The breakdown exists so an agent does not reconstruct the payout rules: in a replace campaign the two sales are not summed. The check re-reads the ledger's verdict, so the case holds even if other passes add conversions to the fixture.

cases.state: seeded fixture; no conversion carries the transaction id EVAL-BD-404
cases.ask: What is the click with the sale EVAL-BD-404 worth, and which of its conversions count?

expected.rubric: PASS if the reply says no conversion with transaction id EVAL-BD-404 was found (so there is no click to explain) and nothing was written. FAIL if it reports a value or a breakdown for any click, or creates a conversion.

cases.notes: The negative of breakdown-001: an unknown id is reported as unknown, grounded in a conversion lookup, never answered with some other click's breakdown.
